name: Meander Migration
desc: A lowland river writhes across its own floodplain — bends grow and crawl downstream under upstream-weighted curvature until a neck closes and severs a loop into an oxbow lake, and every channel position it ever held is printed into the plate as arcuate scroll bars in the ink of its era, so a whole alluvial history accretes and is slowly buried; Fisk alluvial plate, false-colour satellite, sepia survey sheet or cyanotype schematic.

energy.doc: bend migration vigour + colour/contrast gain in the belt inks and thalweg

scale.doc: magnification into the reach around x/y — 1 shows the whole floodplain, 2.6 crops to a single bend

speed.doc: migration rate — how fast bends grow and cut off (0.2 still visibly crawls)

density.doc: floodplain memory: how many scroll-bar generations survive overbank burial, and how many oxbows are retained

discharge.doc: channel width — a creek at 0.05, a trunk river at 1

hue.doc: water/ink hue anchor; rotates the plate inks with it

x.doc: view centre x (only bites when scale > 1)

y.doc: view centre y (only bites when scale > 1)

style.doc: aesthetic: fisk = alluvial plate, historic belts in saturated plate inks; satellite = false-colour NIR, dark-red vegetation, near-black water, white bars; survey = aged sepia sheet, line over mass, ink hachure; blueprint = cyanotype schematic, pale drafting lines on prussian ground

seed.doc: reach + floodplain erodibility seed (rebuilds the river)
